clue.text: One welcoming boy initially has look round

indicators.note: round says the word for look goes all the way around the boy and the letter that follows

parts.note: to take a gander is British slang for to have a look
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word has

explanation.surface: A friendly lad at first takes a good look about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' reads as a verb, but it is British slang for a look, a gander, which goes round the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A glad-hander greets people with effusive, often insincere, handshakes and welcomes.

clue.text: Business that has prices set to tumble

definitions.text: Business that has prices set to tumble

parts.words: Business that has prices set to tumble
parts.note: reads like a firm facing a price crash, but the tumbling is done by clothes in the drying machines of a coin-operated washing shop

explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated laundry is a business whose dryers are set to tumble the washing.

clue.text: Very competitive Dad got ego massaged

indicators.note: massaged means worked over and kneaded, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A father's vanity is flattered, making him fiercely competitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat situation where everyone fights ruthlessly for themselves is called this.

clue.text: Inability to recall men lost in huge landmass

indicators.note: in places the jumbled men inside the name of the huge landmass

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent

indicators.note: lost suggests the men have gone astray, so their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Men going missing in a vast continent cannot remember the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge landmass' is a continent, not an island; the anagram of MEN made by 'lost' is MNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the medical condition named here.

clue.text: Unequal fighters — one stone proved decisive

definitions.text: Unequal fighters — one stone proved decisive

parts.words: Unequal fighters — one stone proved decisive
parts.note: reads like a boxing mismatch decided by a stone's weight, but refers to the Bible story where a shepherd boy fells a giant with a sling-stone

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical shepherd boy and the Philistine giant are the classic mismatched combatants.

clue.text: Fretted wood in colourful setting

indicators.note: in, with setting, says the timber is placed within the colour

parts.note: red is a vivid colour, so colourful gives red
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A carved piece of timber is mounted in a brightly painted frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fretted' suggests ornamental fretwork, but it means worried.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain discontentedly, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Monarch captured by larger than usual resistance units

indicators.note: captured by says the monarch's letters are held inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, larger than usual
HM stands for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A king is seized by unusually big electrical units.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Religious adherent getting back to university

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: A believer returns to college.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the main faith of India is an adherent of that religion.

clue.text: Woman on this wanting husband in her own interests?

indicators.note: in puts the husband's letter into the word for her own interests

parts.note: self means one's own interests, as in self-interest

explanation.surface: A single woman, lacking a husband, looks after herself.
explanation.walkthrough: A woman 'on the shelf' is an old idiom for one thought past marrying age, hence 'wanting husband'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom on the shelf describes a woman left unmarried, so this is the ledge she sits on.

clue.text: Admission for press into free play rejected as author

indicators.note: into, after admission for, says the pressing word goes inside the other piece
rejected means thrown back, so the word for free play is read backwards

parts.note: to give vent is to give free play to a feeling
to urge someone is to press them

explanation.surface: Granting entry to the press, a free play is turned down by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns VENT into TNEV, and URGE goes into it: T + URGE + NEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Power shown by cat's jump

parts.note: the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat leaps powerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring suddenly onto prey is the verb meant; the noun is a sudden leap too.

clue.text: Negotiate, breaking one's principles

indicators.note: breaking says the dealing word splits one's into two parts

parts.note: one is I, plus the S of the possessive
to deal is to negotiate or do business

explanation.surface: Agreeing a compromise, someone breaks their own moral code.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards of conduct or perfection one holds to are one's guiding beliefs.

clue.text: Almost fine collar — spoilt by this?

definitions.text: Almost fine collar — spoilt by this?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for fine loses its final letter

parts.note: dandy means fine or excellent
a ruff is a pleated frilled collar

explanation.surface: A nearly elegant neck frill is ruined by something falling from the scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: DANDY less its last letter gives DAND, then RUFF. The whole clue describes the flakes that would spoil a fine dark collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of dead scalp skin landing on a collar would spoil its look.

clue.text: Bit of fish to eat — picture a dab

parts.note: a fish finger is a breaded strip of fish
a print is a picture

explanation.surface: Eat a bit of fish, and picture a flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: A dab looks like the flatfish of the surface, but 'dabs' is British slang for these impressions taken by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang calls the mark left by a fingertip a dab.

clue.text: Push for basic part of education in school

indicators.note: in places the educational letter inside the school of whales

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
R, from the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Pressure for the basics of learning in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or push someone.

clue.text: In advancing years, an undersized vehicle carries no fare

indicators.note: carries means the small car has the other pieces loaded on in front of it

parts.note: taken as written
to fare is to do, as in how did you do
a Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A small car takes no paying passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts NO and DO ahead of MINI. The Latin for 'in the year of our Lord' is used in Britain as humorous slang for old age.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is colloquial for old age, the advancing of one's years.

clue.text: Upset, removing son'that's run badly

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of removing and the son's letter are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disturbed at taking the boy away, things are managed poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' looks like a deletion signal, but it is anagram fodder: REMOVING plus S rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern a country badly is to rule it poorly.

clue.text: Actor's nerves heartlessly revealed as audience left?

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the eleven-letter phrase is removed

parts.note: stage fright is a performer's nervous fear

explanation.surface: A performer's jitters are cruelly exposed while spectators walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: The right of the stage, from an actor facing the house, is the audience's left; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions are given from the performer's view, so their right side is the spectators' left.

clue.text: Tell composer writing part of Macbeth to add minim in the middle

parts.note: Ross is a Scottish thane, a role in Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: in the middle asks for the letters of minim without the first and last

explanation.surface: A composer writing a role from the Scottish play adds a short note at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' is not the verb: the composer wrote the opera William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini composed the opera William Tell.

clue.text: After' light 'blow, fell over in bar

indicators.note: after says the reversed hill word follows the blow

parts.note: a tap is a light blow

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for fell is read backwards

parts.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Following a gentle punch, someone falls down in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns MOOR into ROOM. 'fell' looks like a verb but is the northern English noun for upland.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the bar of a pub or inn where drinks are served.

clue.text: Unnamed woman had joined cast

parts.note: she refers to a woman without naming her
'd is the contracted form of had, joined on

explanation.surface: An anonymous woman had joined the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin.

clue.text: Dream that's disappeared — Sarah gets annulment

indicators.note: disappeared says the abbreviation for that is has gone from the dream

parts.note: a reverie is a daydream
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
Sal is a pet form of Sarah

explanation.surface: Sarah's dream has vanished and she gets her marriage cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Overturning a decision or judgment is a revocation of it.

clue.text: The diminutive Kipling might have been called healthily tanned

definitions.text: The diminutive Kipling might have been called
definitions.meaning: Rudyard Kipling's first name could be shortened to a pet form

explanation.surface: A pet name for the writer of The Jungle Book would suit a sun-browned face.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish glowing face suggests good health, and the pet form of Rudyard fits too.

clue.text: Curtailment of sin a responsibility primarily for him?

definitions.text: Curtailment of sin a responsibility primarily for him?

indicators.note: curtailment means cutting off the tail, so the word for sin loses its last letter

parts.note: vice is wickedness or sin

indicators.note: primarily asks for only the first letter of responsibility

explanation.surface: Restraining wrongdoing is chiefly the job of a parish priest.
explanation.walkthrough: VICE cut short gives VIC, then A and R (the first letter of 'responsibility'). The whole clue describes a priest's role.
explanation.definitionFit: A Church of England parish priest has curbing sin among his duties.

clue.text: Ready to take part when boisterous game is introduced

indicators.note: is introduced means the game is put into the short form of part

parts.note: a romp is a lively, boisterous game

explanation.surface: Someone eager to join in as a rowdy game starts up.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means quick and ready to act.

clue.text: Half the choir fancied moving after leader left

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leader left means the first letter of fancied departs

explanation.surface: After the conductor departed, half the singers felt emotional about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Without F, FANCIED leaves ANCIED, which 'moving' rearranges. Decani is the dean's side of a cathedral choir, opposite cantoris.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cathedral the singers are split into two sides, one being the dean's side.

clue.text: Run in a bunch of spies, uncovered by the crown in this state

definitions.text: uncovered by the crown in this state

indicators.note: in puts the running word inside the a and the spy agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: Running into a group of agents, the monarch is left exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' is the top of the head, not a monarch's crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair loss leaves the top of the head bare, the condition described.

clue.text: Thirsty, about to swallow a long drink of ale

indicators.note: to swallow means the a is taken inside the reversed thirsty word
about means turned around, so the word for thirsty is read backwards

parts.note: dry means thirsty

explanation.surface: A thirsty drinker is ready to down a long glass of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DRY into YRD, which takes in A: Y + A + RD. A yard of ale is a tall glass about a yard long.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a very tall drinking glass, and its contents.

clue.text: Suppressing busy activity is folly and' callousness

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the folly word contains the busy activity

parts.note: inanity is silliness or folly
a hum of activity is busy goings-on

explanation.surface: Stifling energetic activity is foolish and cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruelty and lack of compassion are what this word for heartlessness means.
